systems.name: Deterministic Quantitative Model
systems.tagline: Turns eight economic-data surprises into return forecasts with a statistical model.
systems.summary: A statistical model turns 8 economic-data surprises into 1-month forecasts.
steps: Measures how far 8 US data releases beat or missed forecasts
A shrinkage regression (Ridge) turns those surprises into 1-month return forecasts
Black–Litterman blends the forecasts with a 45/35/20 starting mix
systems.model: Ridge regression, refit every month on past data only

systems.name: Agentic Workflow — JEV
systems.tagline: JEV, an AI decision model, answers whether stocks will beat bonds over 12 months, and its answer tilts the portfolio.
systems.summary: JEV, an AI decision model, makes a 12-month stocks-versus-bonds call that tilts a 60/40 portfolio.
steps: JEV reads a snapshot of recent market conditions
It gives the chance that stocks beat bonds over 12 months, plus a five-way tilt
The tilt, scaled by JEV's confidence, moves a 60/40 portfolio within 40–80% stocks
signals: Rate levels and a 10-year rate shock
systems.model: JEV decision model (saved answers; version not recorded)

systems.name: Agentic Causal RAG
systems.tagline: Agents propose cause-and-effect hypotheses from economic research and test them against dated evidence.
systems.summary: AI agents propose cause-and-effect hypotheses from research and test them on dated evidence.
steps: A research knowledge graph suggests how this month's events could move markets
A Hypothesis Agent proposes testable hypotheses; a Testing Agent checks them against dated documents and market data
A calibration model turns tested hypotheses into forecasts; Black–Litterman sets the weights
signals: Research knowledge graph (papers dated before each year)
Fed and official documents published before each decision

variants.name: Agentic Workflow — Agent Committee
variants.tagline: A within-approach variant: three AI agents debate the market, and a chief investment officer sets the view.
steps: An Economist and a Risk Manager each read the same market snapshot as JEV
A CIO agent weighs both and states 12-month return views with a confidence level
Black–Litterman tilts a 60/40 portfolio toward the views, more when confidence is high

economist.text: The high cash and long-term yields suggest a challenging environment for both equities and bonds, with economic and geopolitical uncertainties further weighing on risk assets. Given the negative term spread and recent rate shock, TLT may face continued pressure, while SPY's recent drawdown and volatility indicate limited upside potential.

risk_manager.text: The high volatility and significant drawdowns in both SPY and TLT, coupled with elevated economic and geopolitical risks, suggest heightened downside and tail risk. The positive correlation between SPY and TLT reduces diversification benefits, increasing the portfolio's vulnerability to adverse market conditions.

example.cio_rationale: I sided with the Economist on SPY, as the recent drawdown and volatility suggest limited upside, but with the Risk Manager on TLT, given the heightened downside risk and lack of diversification benefits. The combination of high yields, economic uncertainty, and positive correlation between SPY and TLT supports a cautious stance on both assets.

base.name: Base model: 8 economic-data surprises
base.detail: The Deterministic model as it runs in the primary comparison.

variants.name: Add one financial signal at a time
variants.detail: Credit spread, its 3-month change, yield-curve slope, a volatility premium, or 12-month momentum, each added on its own, on the development months. Resumed and completed on 29 Oct 2026 after a written decision and a pre-registration.

result.headline: None of the five improves the forecasts
result.learned: Added one at a time to the 8 economic surprises, no financial signal makes the forecasts better by enough to rule out chance, and none passes the pre-set robustness rule. Every one of them lowers net CER.

rows.label: Largest improvement of the five (credit spread level)
rows.note: p = 0.13; 0.53 after correcting for the five

rows.label: Signals that pass the robustness rule
rows.note: needs significance, the same sign in both halves and 2 of 3 assets

rows.label: Effect on net CER vs the baseline

variants.name: All five financial signals together
variants.detail: The only defined signal set: the 8 surprises plus all five financial signals. The pre-declared conventional-signal test.

result.headline: The combined signal set does not beat the baseline
result.learned: All five financial signals together make the forecasts slightly worse than the 8 economic surprises alone, well within what chance could produce. This was the pre-declared test for conventional signals, and it fails.

rows.label: Signal coverage
rows.note: every signal available in all 46 months, for all three funds

variants.name: Market regimes
variants.detail: Results split by period and by how volatile markets were at the decision date. Both splits were fixed before scoring and use only information available at each decision.

result.headline: Everything earns less after 2019, and none of the approaches is more defensive
result.learned: Split by period and by market volatility at the decision date. All four strategies earn far less per year from 2020 onward at two to three times the volatility, and none of them holds up better than the passive portfolio when volatility is already high.

rows.label: Highest net CER in stressed months
rows.note: 7.66% across 26 months with VIX at or above 20

result.caution: One cell stands out: JEV beats the Deterministic model by +3.67 points in 2019 (p = 0.01), but that is 10 months, one of eight cells, with no correction for looking at several. These splits are diagnostics and never select anything.

base.name: JEV only
base.detail: JEV represents the Agentic Workflow in the primary comparison.

variants.name: Agent Committee only
variants.detail: Three AI agents debate; a chief investment officer sets 12-month views. Compared only with JEV.

variants.name: Committee + JEV
variants.detail: Holds the average of what the Committee and JEV each chose: same months, same two funds, no settings to tune. The rule was fixed in advance.

result.headline: The combination lands between its two parts, and beats neither
result.learned: Holding the average of the Committee's and JEV's choices gives a slightly smoother ride than JEV alone, but it trades much more, and the extra cost cancels the benefit. Combining the two agentic systems is neither better nor worse than either alone.

base.name: Agentic Causal RAG
base.detail: Research graph, Hypothesis and Testing Agents, calibration. Its primary version is chosen before the test opens.

variants.name: Causal RAG — Reduced Evidence
variants.detail: Same agents and steps; the Testing Agent weighs research findings and market and economic data known at each decision. Built and checked end to end. Its first free real-model run (Qwen3 4B) failed the reliability checks; a rerun with fixes is pending.

result.headline: Ran end to end on genuine agent outputs; the gates still failed
result.learned: All 95 agent months produced real qwen3:4b outputs and the 46 development months went through the native pipeline. Its net CER is the highest of the three, and none of that is statistically supported. The permutation placebo puts the genuine agent features near the bottom of the random distribution, so the evidence does not support reading this as forecast skill.

rows.label: Net CER
rows.note: vs Deterministic +1.46 pts, p = 0.47: not statistically clear

rows.label: Months with at least one hypothesis
rows.note: 2021-08 produced none and falls back to its prior

rows.label: Permutation placebo percentile
rows.note: the genuine features beat only 3.5% of 200 random relabelings

result.caution: Both pre-registered reliability gates failed (G3b accuracy 0.5667 with 2 opposite-direction errors; G3a schema-valid call rate 0.9771). This is a diagnostic of the pipeline, not evidence that the agents are reliable or that AI adds investment value.

det.label: Economic surprises
det.text: How far 8 US releases (jobs, retail sales, industrial production, ISM, CPI, core CPI, PPI, hourly earnings) beat or missed forecasts.

det.label: Ridge regression
det.text: A linear model, refit every month on past months only, turns the surprises into return forecasts. It shrinks weak signals toward zero.

det.label: 1-month forecasts
det.text: Expected return above cash for stocks, Treasuries and corporate bonds next month.

det.label: Black–Litterman
det.text: Starts from 45% stocks, 35% Treasuries, 20% corporate bonds and tilts toward the forecasts, within fixed limits.

jev.label: Market snapshot
jev.text: Recent returns, volatility, rates, the term spread, uncertainty indexes and the cash yield, with calendar dates removed.

jev.label: JEV decision model
jev.text: An AI model answers one question each month: will stocks beat bonds over the next 12 months? Its saved answers are replayed exactly.

jev.label: Probability and tilt
jev.text: The chance stocks win, a five-way tilt and a confidence level.

jev.label: Capped tilt
jev.text: Moves a 60% stocks, 40% long-Treasury portfolio between 40% and 80% stocks, more when JEV is confident.

rag.label: Event packet
rag.text: This month's data surprises, Fed meetings and large market moves, all public before 8 p.m. on decision day.

rag.label: Knowledge graph
rag.text: Cause-and-effect findings from economics papers. Each year sees only papers published before it.

rag.label: Hypothesis Agent
rag.text: Proposes up to 6 testable hypotheses a month about how the events could move markets, citing research pathways.

rag.label: CauseTrace graph search
rag.text: CauseTrace: the tools the agent uses to search the graph for pathways and pull the research behind each link.

rag.label: Testing Agent
rag.text: Tries to disprove each hypothesis three times against the evidence available at the time and a rival explanation. Too little evidence means Insufficient, never support.

rag.label: Calibration
rag.text: Learns from past months only how much Supported and Contradicted hypotheses moved returns, and turns them into forecasts.

rag.label: Black–Litterman
rag.text: Same allocation as the Deterministic model: a 45/35/20 starting mix tilted toward the forecasts.

com.label: Market snapshot
com.text: The same snapshot JEV reads, with calendar dates removed.

com.label: Economist + Risk Manager
com.text: Two AI agents write independent views of the outlook.

com.label: Chief investment officer
com.text: A third agent weighs both and sets 12-month return views with a confidence level.

com.label: Black–Litterman
com.text: Tilts a 60/40 portfolio toward the views, more when confidence is high.

det.name: Historical data
det.what: 8 US macro releases against the forecasts that preceded them, plus credit spreads, the yield curve, a variance-risk proxy and 12-month momentum.
det.out: A point-in-time panel ending at the decision date.

det.name: Signal generation
det.what: Each release becomes a standardised surprise (z-score) using only data available before the decision.

det.name: Forecasting
det.what: Ridge regression, refit every month on past months only, with the penalty chosen by inner cross-validation. It may choose the intercept alone.
det.out: A one-month expected excess return per asset.

det.name: Portfolio allocation
det.what: Black–Litterman: the forecast enters as the view q against the equilibrium prior π; the posterior μ_BL feeds a bounded fully invested optimiser.
det.out: Target weights for SPY, IEF and LQD.

det.name: Trades & returns
det.what: Weights are traded at the entry close against the drifted pre-trade weights, at 5 bp per dollar traded, and held to the exit close.
det.out: Turnover, cost and the month's realised return.

det.name: Performance evaluation
det.what: Net of cost and the cash rate, the month joins the 46-month development series scored by the shared evaluator.
det.out: Net excess return, and its place in net CER, volatility and drawdown.

jev.name: Historical data
jev.what: The point-in-time market and macro context available at the decision cut-off.
jev.out: The month's context packet for the agent.

jev.name: Signal generation
jev.what: The agent answers with a probability over five tilt choices, a probability that stocks beat bonds, and its own confidence.
jev.out: A five-way distribution, a choice and a confidence.

jev.name: Forecasting
jev.what: The distribution is averaged into one offset in points of edge, then multiplied by the agent's confidence.

jev.name: Portfolio allocation
jev.what: edge = baseEdge + confidence x offset drives the native capped tilt; the stock weight is clipped to 40-80%.
jev.out: Target weights for SPY and TLT.

jev.name: Trades & returns
jev.what: The same shared evaluator: traded at the entry close against drifted weights at 5 bp per dollar traded.
jev.out: Turnover, cost and the month's realised return.

jev.name: Performance evaluation
jev.what: Net of cost and the cash rate, scored on the same 46 development months as every other approach.
jev.out: Net excess return, and its place in net CER, volatility and drawdown.

rag.name: Historical data
rag.what: Point-in-time evidence: the CauseTrace knowledge graph filtered to the decision year, and the research library.
rag.out: An evidence pool with no post-decision material.

rag.name: Hypothesis & testing agents
rag.what: The Hypothesis Agent proposes causal pathways; the Testing Agent assesses each against retrieved evidence as Supported, Contradicted or Insufficient.

rag.name: Signal encoding & forecasting
rag.what: Categorical assessments are encoded as status features and calibrated, walk-forward, into a numerical view.

rag.name: Portfolio allocation
rag.what: The native Causal RAG allocation over SPY, IEF and LQD.

rag.name: Trades & returns
rag.what: The same shared evaluator and costs as the other approaches.

rag.name: Performance evaluation
rag.what: Scored on the same development months, once the reliability gates pass.
rag.out: Net excess return and the development metrics.

entries.title: Why every Causal RAG figure is marked exploratory
entries.what: Its agents did not pass the two pre-registered reliability gates: G3b (accuracy 0.5666666666666667, opposite direction errors 2); G3a (schema valid call rate 0.9770642201834863). The thresholds were set before the run and were not changed. Every Causal RAG number in this dashboard is therefore a diagnostic of the pipeline, not validated evidence that the agents are reliable or that AI adds investment value. No contrast involving it is statistically clear, and its permutation placebo places the genuine agent features near the bottom of the random distribution.

entries.title: Calibration and placebo diagnostics
entries.what: Intercept-only share, calibration slope and the permutation placebo that argues against predictive content.
